rationale: B wins because it knows when to stop. Its best line is the unpleasant one: "Fastest-growing channel off a base of zero is trivially true" — that is the reporter objection a founder needs to solve before pitching. A has more range, but "For Kohl's shoppers, Glossier is now something you walk into, not a website you order from" starts building a shopper-impact story before it has markets, stocking details, or evidence that online availability was the barrier.
gaps_in_A: "For Kohl's shoppers, Glossier is now something you walk into, not a website you order from" overstates access; DTC shoppers could already order online, so the real story needs location, sampling, or discovery proof.

"Sephora at Kohl's becomes a test case for prestige beauty in a big-box mall" is a little grand for one brand expansion; "test case" needs broader Sephora-at-Kohl's evidence before it can carry that weight.
"previously online-only or coastal-urban" smuggles in "coastal-urban" without support from the update.
The next step says "five viable shapes exist"; three are clearly viable, two are promising but still under-proved.
gaps_in_B: "quietly became a wholesale company" overclaims the fact block; fastest-growing channel does not mean wholesale is the company's main business.
"collapse of the direct-to-consumer thesis" is too sweeping unless B can bring outside comparables; Glossier alone does not collapse a thesis.
"wave of beauty brands extending into scent" is plausible trade context, but it is not in the update and needs sourced examples before pitching.
B misses the sharper Sephora-at-Kohl's channel lens; it keeps the set clean, but leaves one potentially useful retail-trade angle on the floor.
